newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by continued weak pork prices, livestock dealers said.
However, prices were seen stabilizing following recent steep declines on ideas that hog supplies were slowing as producers get more current in their marketings.
Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for the bulk of hogs delivered to the plant could range from $51.50 to $52.00, with a few top quality hogs at $54.00.
Illinois top prices at plants could range from $51.00 to $51.50, sources there said.
Indiana and Ohio hog prices Thursday were seen off $0.50, with a top range at plants of $50.50 to $51.00.
This week's active pork production pace also weighed on wholesale prices but the lower prices were starting to do the job of moving product, market sources said.

Midday carlot pork prices were lower, but 50.0 loads of pork and 5.0 loads of trimmings were reported sold, USDA said. Some market sources said the movement was promising for midday sales, particularly following Tuesday's trade of 99.0 pork loads and 37.0 loads of trimmings.
